Former Jewish Prayer Room in Schwetzingen

Former Synagogue · Schwetzingen, Germany

From 1864 to around 1897, the small Jewish community of Schwetzingen, which numbered no more than ten to twelve families and included Jewish residents of nearby Ketsch, held services in a prayer room inside a house at what is now Invalidengasse 6. A dedicated synagogue building was proposed as early as 1808 but never built for lack of funds. After 1897 the congregation used rooms in Schwetzingen Palace and later private homes. The street, historically called Synagogenstraße, was renamed Invalidengasse by the Nazi regime in 1934; in 2015 the city restored a reference to the earlier name on the street sign alongside an informational plaque.
